finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.assumptions: The code does not sanitize the filename input before using it in an OS call, and the environment allows shell interpretation.

parsed.refutation_attempt: The code calls std::ifstream(filename) to open a file. This function internally uses the OS open(2) system call with the exact string supplied as the file path; it does not invoke a shell or parse shell metacharacters. Since the sink is a file-open operation rather than a command execution, the presence of characters such as ';' or '|' in the filename cannot trigger command injection. No subsequent system() or exec* call is made that would interpret the filename as a command. Therefore the reported OS Command Injection vulnerability cannot occur in this fragment.

finding.title: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
finding.trigger: filename containing special elements like wildcards (e.g., *)
finding.assumptions: The code does not sanitize the filename input before using it in an OS call, and the environment allows shell interpretation.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked whether the filename is passed to a system shell command; it is used only in ifstream(filename) which opens a file directly without invoking a shell. No check is required as no command execution occurs. The source (cin >> filename) is untrusted, but the sink does not lead to OS command execution. The presence of wildcards in the filename does not trigger globbing in ifstream. Thus the CWE-76 claim is invalid.
